scenario: 面试题：设计 GitHub Copilot 这类代码补全产品背后的 ML 系统。
scenario_en: Interview prompt: design the ML system behind a code-completion product like GitHub Copilot.
q: 设计代码补全系统的核心张力（defining tension）是什么？
q_en: What is the defining tension when designing a code-completion system?
why: 三方拉扯：快到让人感觉「隐形」（sub-200ms）、准到值得信任、私到能处理专有源码。这不是纯建模题，而是要在极致延迟、IDE 上下文检索、隐私敏感数据、多入口需求之间平衡的系统设计题。
why_en: The tension is being fast enough to feel invisible, accurate enough to earn trust, and private enough for proprietary source code — a full system design problem, not just modeling.
diagram:
flowchart TD T["核心张力"] --> F["快到隐形
sub-200ms"] T --> A["准到可信"] T --> P["私到可处理专有码"]
options: 只在模型精度 vs 训练成本之间取舍，其余都是工程细节
只在支持多少种编程语言之间权衡
快到隐形、准到可信、私到能处理专有源码——三者同时满足
只在用云端还是本地部署之间二选一
options_en: Only trade off model accuracy vs training cost; the rest is engineering detail.
Only weigh how many programming languages to support.
Fast enough to feel invisible, accurate enough to earn trust, private enough for proprietary code — all at once.
Only choose between cloud or on-device deployment.
optionExplanations: 精度 vs 成本只是其中一角，忽略了延迟、隐私、多入口这些同样致命的约束。
语言覆盖是子问题，撑不起「隐形/可信/私密」三方同时拉扯的核心张力。
对；速度、准确、隐私三者互相牵制，是这道题区别于纯建模题的系统设计内核。
云 vs 本地只是隐私约束的一个后果，不是问题的核心张力本身。
optionExplanations_en: Accuracy vs cost is one corner, ignoring latency, privacy, and multi-surface constraints that are equally fatal.
Language coverage is a sub-problem and can't carry the core three-way invisible/trusted/private tension.
Correct — speed, accuracy, and privacy constrain each other, the systems-design core that sets this apart from pure modeling.
Cloud vs on-device is a consequence of the privacy constraint, not the core tension itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在开发者编码时预测并建议接下来的代码，如 Copilot 的 ghost text。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Code completion predicts and suggests upcoming code as a developer types, like Copilot's ghost text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 知识产权，这里指用户的专有源代码，属敏感资产。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP (Intellectual Property) here means the user's proprietary source code, a sensitive asset.

scenario: 开场要先列全产品的所有补全入口，再挑一个深挖。
scenario_en: You should first enumerate all the product's completion surfaces, then pick one to deep-dive.
q: 代码补全产品的四个 completion surface（补全入口）是哪些？
q_en: What are the four completion surfaces of a code-completion product?
why: 四个入口：inline（边打边出的 ghost text）、chat（自然语言→多文件）、单测生成、文档生成。四者的触发方式、延迟预算和质量信号都不同。
why_en: The four surfaces are inline ghost text, chat-based generation, unit-test generation, and documentation generation, each with its own trigger, latency budget, and quality signal.
options: 只有 inline 补全存在，其余三个都只是它换了层皮的变体
inline 补全、chat 生成、单测生成、文档生成
代码搜索、错误诊断、自动重构建议、代码审查评论
语法高亮显示、编辑器自动缩进、括号自动匹配、实时拼写检查
options_en: Only inline completion exists; the other three are just its variants wearing a different skin.
Inline completion, chat generation, unit-test generation, doc generation.
Code search, error diagnosis, automated refactor suggestions, code review comments.
Syntax highlighting, editor auto-indent, bracket auto-matching, real-time spell check.
optionExplanations: 四个入口在触发和约束上差异很大，chat/单测/文档生成并不是 inline 换皮的变体。
对；这四个入口各有触发方式、延迟预算和质量信号，是 scoping 的出发点。
代码搜索、错误诊断、重构建议、代码审查是辅助开发工具，不是模型生成代码的入口。
语法高亮、自动缩进、括号匹配、拼写检查是编辑器内置基础功能，不涉及 ML 代码生成。
optionExplanations_en: The four surfaces differ greatly in triggers and constraints; chat/test-gen/docs aren't inline wearing a different skin.
Correct — these four each have distinct triggers, latency budgets, and quality signals, the starting point for scoping.
Code search, error diagnosis, refactor suggestions, and code review are dev-assist tools, not the model's code-generation surfaces.
Highlighting/indenting/matching/spellcheck are built-in editor basics, not ML code generation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 产品向用户提供代码生成的一种交互形态（inline、chat、test、docs）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A completion surface is one interaction form the product offers for code generation (inline, chat, test, docs).

scenario: 时间有限，要在四个补全入口里挑一个深挖，展示最有意思的架构取舍。
scenario_en: With limited time, pick one of the four surfaces to deep-dive and show the most interesting architectural trade-offs.
q: 深挖时通常该选哪个 surface，为什么？
q_en: Which surface should you usually deep-dive, and why?
why: 选 inline suggestions：它延迟预算最紧（sub-200ms）、触发最频繁、且要从纯键盘输入推断意图（没有显式指令），架构上最有挑战也最能体现取舍。其他入口延迟宽松、有显式请求，反而没那么吃系统设计功力。
why_en: Pick inline suggestions — the tightest latency (sub-200ms), highest frequency, and it must infer intent from keystrokes alone, making it the most architecturally interesting.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确想聊「自然语言到多文件代码」的能力或 agentic 生成，那 chat-based 才是该深挖的入口。
options: documentation generation，因为写文档最简单
inline suggestions，延迟最紧、频率最高、要推断隐式意图
test generation，因为它有明确的通过/失败信号，比其余三个入口更容易评估质量
随便挑哪个都行，反正四个入口的触发方式、延迟预算和架构本质上完全一样
options_en: Documentation generation, because writing docs is easiest.
Inline suggestions — tightest latency, highest frequency, must infer implicit intent.
Test generation, because it has a clear pass/fail signal, making quality easier to evaluate than the other three surfaces.
Any of them — the four surfaces are basically identical in trigger, latency budget, and architecture anyway.
optionExplanations: 简单不是深挖理由，文档生成延迟宽松、约束少，展示不出系统设计取舍。
对；sub-200ms + 隐式意图推断让 inline 的架构约束最强，最能展开取舍讨论。
有通过信号确实好评估，但 test 生成延迟宽松（5–15s），不是最吃延迟架构、最考验取舍的入口。
四者延迟、触发、隐私约束差别很大，说触发方式和架构完全一样是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Easy isn't a reason to deep-dive; docs have loose latency and few constraints, showing little systems trade-off.
Correct — sub-200ms plus implicit intent inference make inline the most constrained and richest for discussing trade-offs.
A pass signal is nice for evaluation, but test gen has loose latency (5–15s), not the most latency-critical, trade-off-rich surface.
The four differ greatly in latency, triggers, and privacy, so claiming identical trigger and architecture is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开发者边打字边以 ghost text 预测接下来 1–3 行代码的入口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inline suggestions predict the next 1–3 lines as ghost text while the developer types.

scenario: 对比 inline 建议和 chat 生成两种入口，好决定各自的延迟目标和正确性要求。
scenario_en: Comparing inline suggestions and chat-based generation to set each surface's latency target and correctness bar.
q: inline suggestions 与 chat-based generation 在触发、延迟、正确性上如何不同？
q_en: How do inline suggestions and chat-based generation differ in trigger, latency, and correctness?
why: inline 由键入隐式触发、预算 <200ms、输出 1–3 行；chat 由显式提问触发、可等几秒、输出多文件但正确性要求更严。触发的显隐决定两边档位。
why_en: Inline is triggered implicitly by keystrokes with a <200ms budget and 1–3 line output, while chat is an explicit NL request tolerating seconds but demanding stricter correctness.
tradeoff: inline（隐式触发、<200ms、宽松正确性）vs chat（显式请求、秒级、严正确性）
options: inline 由显式提问触发、chat 由键入触发，正好相反
两者延迟预算完全相同，都必须控制在 sub-200ms 内，只是输出长度不一样
inline：隐式触发、<200ms；chat：显式请求、秒级更严
chat 只输出 1 行简单代码，inline 才是能一次生成多文件、多行的复杂重构
options_en: Inline is triggered by explicit prompts and chat by keystrokes — exactly reversed.
Both must fit the same sub-200ms budget and differ only in output length.
Inline: implicit trigger, <200ms; chat: explicit request, seconds but stricter.
Chat only outputs 1 simple line, while inline is the one that generates complex multi-file, multi-line refactors.
optionExplanations: 触发方向搞反了：inline 才是隐式键入，chat 才是显式提问。
延迟预算差一个数量级：inline <200ms，chat 可到 2–10s，不可能都控制在 sub-200ms 内。
对；显式请求容忍更长延迟但要求更准，隐式建议要极快但可被随手忽略，档位不同。
反了：inline 才是输出 1–3 行的简单建议，chat 才产多行/多文件的复杂重构。
optionExplanations_en: Trigger direction reversed: inline is implicit keystroke, chat is explicit prompt.
The budgets differ by an order of magnitude: inline <200ms, chat 2–10s — they can't both fit sub-200ms.
Correct — an explicit request tolerates more latency but demands accuracy, while implicit suggestions must be instant but are easily ignored.
Reversed: inline is the one outputting 1–3 simple lines, while chat produces the multi-line/multi-file refactors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户用自然语言显式提出需求，模型生成多行或多文件代码块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Chat-based generation takes an explicit natural-language request and produces multi-line or multi-file code.

scenario: 对比不同入口对上下文的需求：test generation 入口该拿到什么才做得好。
scenario_en: Comparing each surface's context needs: what test generation needs to work well.
q: test generation 入口要产出好用的单元测试，需要哪些输入信息？
q_en: What inputs does test generation need to produce useful unit tests?
why: test 生成要看到目标函数/类的签名、要覆盖的边界情况，以及项目用的测试框架（pytest / JUnit 等），否则生成的测试跑不起来或不符合项目约定。它是显式命令触发、延迟宽松（5–15s），质量看测试通过率和覆盖率增量。
why_en: It needs the target's signatures, the edge cases to cover, and the project's testing framework, or the tests won't run or won't match project conventions.
options: 函数签名、要覆盖的边界情况、测试框架
只要函数名就够，其余模型能自己猜全
用户的自然语言描述，无需看代码本身
整个仓库的 git 提交历史
options_en: Function signatures, the edge cases to cover, and the testing framework.
Just the function name is enough; the model guesses the rest.
The user's natural-language description, without seeing the code.
The whole repo's git commit history.
optionExplanations: 对；签名定接口、边界定覆盖、框架定语法，三者齐全生成的测试才可跑、可用。
光函数名猜不出参数类型和边界，生成的测试大概率跑不通。
test 生成要基于真实代码，纯自然语言描述无法产出准确断言。
整仓提交历史与生成某个函数的单测无关，属噪声。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — signatures define the interface, edge cases define coverage, framework defines syntax; all three make tests runnable and useful.
The name alone can't reveal parameter types or edges, so generated tests likely won't run.
Test gen must be grounded in real code; a pure NL description can't produce accurate assertions.
The whole commit history is irrelevant noise for generating one function's unit tests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从函数或类自动生成单元测试，需签名、边界与测试框架信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Test generation auto-produces unit tests from a function/class, needing signatures, edge cases, and the test framework.

scenario: documentation generation 和 inline 生成，两者的任务本质不同。
scenario_en: Documentation generation and inline generation differ in the essence of the task.
q: documentation generation 与 inline 代码合成在任务本质上有何不同？
q_en: How does documentation generation differ in essence from inline code synthesis?
why: 文档生成本质是「总结+解释」已有代码（docstring、注释、README），输入是完整代码、输出是自然语言描述；inline 是「合成」尚不存在的代码。前者从代码到解释，后者从上下文到新代码，方向相反。
why_en: Documentation generation summarizes and explains existing code (docstrings, comments, README), while inline synthesizes new code that doesn't exist yet — opposite directions.
tradeoff: docs（总结+解释已有代码）vs inline（从上下文合成新代码）
options: 两者都是从零开始合成全新代码，本质完全一样，没有任何区别
docs 总结解释已有代码，inline 合成新代码，方向相反
docs 生成的延迟要求比 inline 严格得多，必须在几十毫秒内完成
docs 生成需要用户显式给提示词，inline 补全同样需要显式提示词才会触发
options_en: Both synthesize brand-new code from scratch — essentially identical, no difference.
Docs explain existing code, inline synthesizes new code — opposite directions.
Docs have far stricter latency requirements than inline, needing to finish within tens of milliseconds.
Docs need the user to explicitly supply a prompt, and inline completion likewise needs an explicit prompt to trigger.
optionExplanations: 文档生成的输入就是现成代码，不是从零合成，二者本质不同。
对；一个从代码产出解释、一个从上下文产出新代码，任务方向相反。
延迟反了：inline <200ms 才严，docs 3–10s 宽松得多，不是 docs 更严。
inline 是隐式键入触发、无显式提示词，这条说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Doc generation's input is existing code, not scratch synthesis — the two differ in essence.
Correct — one produces explanation from code, the other new code from context: opposite directions.
Latency is reversed: inline <200ms is strict, docs 3–10s are much looser — docs isn't stricter.
Inline is implicit keystroke-triggered with no explicit prompt — this is reversed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从代码生成 docstring、注释或 README，是总结与解释而非合成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Documentation generation produces docstrings, comments, or README from code — summarization and explanation, not synthesis.

scenario: 要给 inline 代码补全定一个主在线指标，衡量建议是否真的被用上。
scenario_en: You must pick a primary online metric for inline completion, measuring whether suggestions are actually used.
q: inline 补全的主在线指标应该是什么？
q_en: What should be the primary online metric for inline completion?
why: accepted completion rate（展示出的 inline 建议被 Tab 接受的比例）是主在线指标：被忽略的建议不仅没价值，还占用注意力、侵蚀信任。它直接反映建议是否有用，健康区间约 25–35%。
why_en: Accepted completion rate — the share of shown inline suggestions accepted via Tab — is primary, because dismissed suggestions waste attention and erode trust.
whenOtherWins: 如果要衡量的是长期商业价值而非单次建议好坏，用户留存(retention)才是终极指标；accepted rate 只是短期在线代理。
options: 模型在 HumanEval 上的 pass@1 离线基准分，衡量训练时的代码生成能力
GPU 集群利用率（基础设施利用效率）
accepted completion rate（接受率）
每天系统生成并展示给用户的建议总条数，反映产量而非建议质量
options_en: The model's offline HumanEval pass@1 benchmark score, measuring training-time code-generation ability.
GPU cluster utilization, i.e. infrastructure efficiency.
Accepted completion rate — the share of shown suggestions accepted.
The total number of suggestions the system generates and shows users per day — volume, not quality.
optionExplanations: HumanEval 是离线能力分，反映不了真实用户是否接受你的建议。
GPU 利用率是基础设施指标，与建议有没有用无关。
对；被接受率直接量化建议是否被采纳，是 inline 的主在线指标（健康约 25–35%）。
生成总条数只是产量不是质量，狂推没人接受的建议只会拉低信任。
optionExplanations_en: HumanEval is an offline capability score and doesn't reflect whether real users accept your suggestions.
GPU utilization is infrastructure, unrelated to whether suggestions are useful.
Correct — acceptance rate directly quantifies whether suggestions are taken, the primary online metric for inline (healthy ~25–35%).
Total count is just output, not quality; flooding un-accepted suggestions just erodes trust.

termDefinitions.meaning: 展示给用户的 inline 建议中被接受(Tab)的百分比，主在线质量指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Accepted completion rate is the percentage of shown inline suggestions accepted (via Tab), the primary online quality metric.

tradeoff: accepted rate（短期在线代理，能天天看）vs retention（长期商业结果，反馈慢）

scenario: 上线后看 inline 建议的接受率，想知道多少算健康、多少算异常。
scenario_en: After launch you watch inline acceptance rate and want to know what counts as healthy.
q: 填空：inline 建议接受率的健康区间与生产力对照数。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: the healthy inline acceptance range and the productivity anchor.
text: inline 建议的健康接受率约 {{25–35%}}；GitHub 报告用 Copilot 后任务完成约快 {{55%}}。这两个是经验基准，不是公式推导；接受率过高但留存下降，往往是建议过于保守。
text_en: Healthy inline acceptance is about {{25–35%}}; GitHub reported ~{{55%}} faster task completion with Copilot. These are empirical benchmarks, not formulas; very high acceptance with falling retention often means the suggestions are too conservative.
why: 25–35% 是经验健康区间：太低说明建议没用，太高常意味着只推显而易见的补全、生产力反而低。55% 更快是 Copilot 的对照实验结果，用来论证生产力提升，不是任何公式算出来的目标。
why_en: 25–35% is an empirical healthy band — too low means useless, too high often means trivial suggestions — and the 55% figure is Copilot's controlled-experiment result, not a formula.

termDefinitions.meaning: 受控实验里代码补全带来的任务提速、少切换等收益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Productivity lift is the task-speedup and reduced-context-switching gain from code completion, measured in controlled experiments.

scenario: 要在指标层级里排出哪个是终极商业指标。
scenario_en: In the metric hierarchy, you must decide which is the ultimate business metric.
q: 为什么 user retention 被视为代码补全产品的终极商业指标？
q_en: Why is user retention the ultimate business metric for a code-completion product?
why: 留存 = 采用后仍持续使用的用户比例，直接对应长期价值和订阅收入。接受率、生产力提升都是过程指标，最终要落到「用户愿不愿意长期留下来付费」，所以留存是终极商业指标。
why_en: Retention — the share who keep using after adoption — maps directly to long-term value and subscription revenue, the outcome that acceptance and productivity ultimately serve.
options: 因为留存在产品分析后台里最容易统计，报表天然就有这个字段
因为它是采用后持续使用的比例，直连订阅收入
因为留存和接受率在统计意义上完全等价，看哪个指标都一样
因为留存只在产品刚上线的第一周才重要，之后就不用再盯着它了
options_en: Because retention is the easiest field to pull from the product analytics dashboard.
Because it is the share still using after adoption, tied to subscription revenue.
Because retention and acceptance rate are statistically equivalent, so either metric tells you the same thing.
Because retention only matters during the first launch week and can be ignored after that.
optionExplanations: 好不好统计不是它当终极指标的理由，价值指向才是。
对；留存直连长期价值和订阅收入，过程指标最终都要兑现成留存。
两者不等价：接受率可以很高但用户仍流失（建议太保守），留存才见真章。
留存恰恰是长期指标，看的是采用后能否持续用下去，不是只看上线第一周。
optionExplanations_en: Ease of measurement isn't why it's ultimate; pointing at value is.
Correct — retention ties directly to long-term value and subscription revenue, which process metrics must cash out into.
They aren't equivalent: acceptance can be high while users churn (too-conservative suggestions); retention tells the truth.
Retention is precisely a long-term metric about sustained use after adoption, not something to ignore after week one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 采用产品后一段时间仍在使用的用户比例，衡量长期价值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retention is the share of users still using the product some time after adoption, measuring long-term value.

scenario: 某代码补全上线后接受率高达 40%，但用户在第 1 个月后留存明显下降。
scenario_en: A code-completion tool launches with 40% acceptance, but user retention clearly drops after month 1.
q: 接受率 40% 却留存下降，最可能的原因是什么？
q_en: 40% acceptance yet falling retention — what's the most likely cause?
why: 很可能模型只推「显而易见、没什么价值」的补全：这类建议容易被顺手接受，接受率好看，但没真正加速开发，用户新鲜感过后就流失。只优化接受率是陷阱——高接受 + 低留存 = 建议太保守、没交付价值。
why_en: The model likely suggests trivially obvious completions: easy to accept so acceptance looks good, but they don't accelerate development, so users churn once novelty fades.
tradeoff: 只冲接受率（爱推琐碎补全）vs 兼顾留存（敢推有价值但接受率略低的补全）
options: 模型太准了，用户觉得不需要自己写代码而离开
模型只推琐碎补全，接受率好看却没加速开发
接受率太高导致服务器过载，用户被迫离开
留存下降和补全质量无关，纯属季节性波动
options_en: The model is too accurate, so users feel they don't need to write code and leave.
The model only suggests trivial completions: acceptance looks good but work is not faster.
Acceptance is so high it overloads servers, forcing users to leave.
Retention drop is unrelated to completion quality — just seasonal noise.
optionExplanations: 太准不会赶走用户，反而提升留存，这个因果是反的。
对；琐碎补全接受率高但不产生价值，新鲜感一过就留不住人——这正是只看接受率的陷阱。
接受率高不等于服务器过载，两者没有直接因果。
留存和补全是否真加速开发强相关，甩给季节波动是回避分析。
optionExplanations_en: Being too accurate wouldn't drive users away — it would raise retention; the causality is reversed.
Correct — trivial completions get accepted but deliver no value, so users leave once novelty fades — the trap of optimizing acceptance alone.
High acceptance doesn't mean server overload; no direct causal link.
Retention correlates strongly with whether completions truly accelerate work; blaming seasonality dodges the analysis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 显而易见、用户本来就会写的补全，易接受但几乎不提升生产力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trivial completion is obvious code the user would write anyway — easily accepted but barely boosting productivity.

scenario: 团队争论：该让模型多推大胆的多行补全，还是稳妥的短补全。
scenario_en: The team debates whether the model should push bold multi-line completions or safe short ones.
q: 「建议激进度 vs 接受率」这个权衡该怎么把握？
q_en: How should you handle the 'suggestion aggressiveness vs acceptance rate' trade-off?
why: 越激进（多行、有雄心）的建议接受率越低，但一旦被接受生产力提升大；越保守（琐碎）的接受率高却价值小。不能只顾接受率，要盯生产力和留存来平衡激进度——目标是被接受时真能帮上大忙。
why_en: More aggressive multi-line suggestions get lower acceptance but big productivity when accepted, so balance aggressiveness against productivity and retention, not acceptance alone.
whenOtherWins: 若产品定位是「零打扰、只补最稳的一两 token」，保守策略更合适——此时高接受率、低打扰本身就是卖点。
options: 一律最激进，多行大块建议越多越好，无视接受率
一律最保守，只推最稳的琐碎补全，把接受率顶满
用生产力和留存来平衡激进度，而不是只看接受率
激进度和接受率无关，随便设即可
options_en: Always maximally aggressive — the more multi-line blocks the better, ignore acceptance.
Always maximally conservative — push only safe trivial completions to max out acceptance.
Tune aggressiveness against productivity and retention, not acceptance alone.
Aggressiveness is unrelated to acceptance; set it arbitrarily.
optionExplanations: 一味激进会让接受率崩、打扰感强，反噬信任，不是平衡。
一味保守接受率高但生产力和留存低，正是前面说的陷阱。
对；激进与接受率此消彼长，用生产力/留存当准绳去调，才能让被接受的建议真正值钱。
两者强相关（越激进越难被接受），说无关是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Pure aggressiveness crashes acceptance and feels intrusive, hurting trust — not balance.
Pure conservatism maxes acceptance but tanks productivity and retention — exactly the earlier trap.
Correct — aggressiveness and acceptance trade off, so tune by productivity/retention so accepted suggestions truly pay off.
They correlate strongly (more aggressive is harder to accept), so 'unrelated' is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 建议的雄心程度：从一两 token 的稳妥补全到多行大块的大胆补全。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Suggestion aggressiveness is how ambitious a suggestion is, from a safe token or two to bold multi-line blocks.

tradeoff: 激进建议（接受率低但被接受时价值大）vs 保守建议（接受率高但价值小）

scenario: 除了主指标，还要一批次级指标反哺模型迭代和服务调优。
scenario_en: Beyond the primary metric, you want secondary metrics to feed model iteration and serving tuning.
q: 代码补全的有用次级指标包括哪些？(多选)
q_en: Which are useful secondary metrics for code completion? (multiple)
why: 接受后的 edit distance（接受后又改了多少，反映建议贴合度）、延迟 p50/p95/p99（尾延迟影响体验）、代码安全扫描通过率（别推有漏洞的代码）都是有用次级指标，反哺模型迭代与服务调优。生成建议的字符数不是质量信号。
why_en: Post-acceptance edit distance, latency p50/p95/p99, and code security-scan pass rate are useful secondary metrics feeding model iteration and serving tuning.
options: 接受后 edit distance：接受后用户又改了多少
延迟 p50/p95/p99：尾延迟决定是否感觉卡顿
代码安全扫描通过率：别把有漏洞的代码推给用户
建议里包含的字符总数
options_en: Post-acceptance edit distance: how much the user edits after accepting.
Latency p50/p95/p99: tail latency decides whether it feels laggy.
Code security-scan pass rate: don't push vulnerable code to users.
Total character count in the suggestion.
optionExplanations: 对；接受后大改说明建议只是「差不多」，edit distance 是贴合度的敏感信号。
对；p95/p99 尾延迟一旦超阈值就破坏心流，必须监控。
对；推出带漏洞的代码会造成实际危害，安全扫描通过率是必要护栏。
错；字符数是产量不是质量，长建议未必好，不构成有用信号。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — heavy post-accept edits mean the suggestion was only 'close'; edit distance is a sensitive fit signal.
Correct — p95/p99 tail latency past a threshold breaks flow and must be monitored.
Correct — shipping vulnerable code causes real harm, so security-scan pass rate is a needed guardrail.
Wrong — character count is output not quality; a long suggestion isn't necessarily good, so it's no useful signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一段文本改成另一段所需的最少编辑操作数，这里量接受后的改动量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum edits to turn one text into another, here measuring changes after acceptance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 延迟的中位/95/99 百分位；尾百分位反映最差那部分请求的体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p50/p95/p99 are the median/95th/99th latency percentiles; tail percentiles reflect the worst requests' experience.

scenario: 开发者以 50–100 WPM 打字，光标一直在动，你要论证 inline 建议为什么必须 sub-200ms。
scenario_en: Developers type 50–100 WPM with the cursor always moving; justify why inline suggestions must be sub-200ms.
q: 为什么 inline 建议的延迟目标定在 200ms 以内？
q_en: Why is the inline suggestion latency target set under 200ms?
why: 这是给定的产品目标而非公式推导：开发者打字快（50–100 WPM），建议若在光标已经移开后才到就「到即已死」；200ms 对齐人类感知阈值，超过就感觉卡、打断心流。它是 inline 架构最重要的驱动约束，要尽早在面试里点出。
why_en: It's a product target, not a derived number: developers type fast, a suggestion arriving after the cursor moved is dead on arrival, and 200ms aligns with human perception beyond which it feels laggy.
options: 200ms 是 GPU 单次前向传播的固定物理耗时，无论怎么优化都改不了
给定的产品目标：迟到的建议到即已死，超 200ms 打断心流
200ms 是 HTTP 协议明文规定的响应超时上限，服务器必须遵守
这个数字是随便定的，300ms、500ms 用户体验其实感觉不出差别
options_en: 200ms is the fixed physical cost of one GPU forward pass and can't be optimized away.
A given product target: a late suggestion is dead on arrival and past 200ms it breaks flow.
200ms is a response timeout ceiling explicitly mandated by the HTTP protocol that servers must obey.
The number is arbitrary; users can't actually tell 300ms or 500ms apart from it.
optionExplanations: 200ms 不是某次前向的物理常数，它是端到端预算里对人的感知目标。
对；这是产品设定的感知阈值目标，不是算出来的；超过它建议就「到即已死」、破坏心流。
没有任何网络协议规定 200ms，这纯属虚构。
300–500ms 已明显偏慢（开发者会一天内关掉），用户体验差得出来，不是感觉不出差别。
optionExplanations_en: 200ms isn't a physical constant of a forward pass; it's a human-perception target across the whole end-to-end budget.
Correct — it's a product-set perception threshold, not derived; beyond it suggestions are 'dead on arrival' and break flow.
No network protocol mandates 200ms — pure fiction.
300–500ms is clearly sluggish (devs disable it within a day) — users very much can tell the difference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每分钟打字词数，开发者约 50–100，决定建议必须多快到达。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WPM (Words Per Minute) is typing speed; developers hit ~50–100, setting how fast a suggestion must arrive.

termDefinitions.term: dead on arrival / 到即已死
termDefinitions.meaning: 建议到达时光标早已移开、场景已变，价值归零。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dead on arrival means the suggestion lands after the cursor has moved on, so its value is already zero.

scenario: 把 200ms 端到端预算拆成各阶段，好判断留给模型推理多少时间。
scenario_en: Breaking the 200ms end-to-end budget into stages to see how much is left for inference.
q: 填空：inline 请求 200ms 预算的各阶段拆分。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: the inline request's 200ms budget breakdown.
text: 上下文收集(前缀/后缀/开着的标签页){{10–30ms}} + 网络往返 {{20–50ms}}（合计约 30–80ms 在计算前就花掉）+ 模型推理剩下的 {{100–150ms}}（prefill+解码）。所以推理这段最吃紧，逼着用小模型和投机解码。
text_en: Context collection (prefix/suffix/open tabs) {{10–30ms}} + network round-trip {{20–50ms}} (~30–80ms gone before compute) + model inference in the remaining {{100–150ms}} (prefill + decode). Inference is the tightest slice, forcing small models and speculative decoding.
why: 拆预算的意义在于：网络+上下文收集就吃掉 30–80ms，真正留给模型 prefill+解码的只有 100–150ms。这个「余额」直接决定模型大小(1–7B)、要不要投机解码和 KV cache——把数字摆出来，架构选择就顺理成章。
why_en: The breakdown shows network plus context eats 30–80ms, leaving only 100–150ms for inference, which directly forces model size (1–7B), speculative decoding, and KV caching.

termDefinitions.meaning: IDE 插件收集光标前缀、后缀、开着的标签页等，作为请求输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context collection is the IDE plugin gathering prefix, suffix, open tabs, and cursor position as request input.

scenario: 扣掉网络和上下文收集，只剩约 100–150ms 给模型 prefill+解码，要给 inline 选模型规模。
scenario_en: After network and context, only ~100–150ms remain for prefill+decode; choose a model size for inline.
q: sub-200ms 预算把 inline 的模型规模逼到什么范围？
q_en: What model size range does the sub-200ms budget force for inline?
why: 推理窗口只剩 100–150ms，把 inline 逼到 1–7B 小模型，再用投机解码和 KV cache 挤进预算；更大的模型留给延迟宽松的 chat。
why_en: With only 100–150ms for inference, inline is forced to 1–7B models (larger models serve chat), paired with speculative decoding, KV caching, and careful batching.
whenOtherWins: 如果是 chat 入口、延迟能容忍到几秒，就该上更大的模型换更强的正确性，小模型反而不必要地限制质量。
options: 70B+ 大模型，靠堆 GPU 算力硬压延迟
1–7B 小模型 + 投机解码/KV cache
模型越大越好，延迟由缓存全部消化
不用模型，用纯规则模板做补全
options_en: 70B+ models, brute-forcing the latency with more GPU compute.
1–7B small models plus speculative decoding and KV cache.
The bigger the better; caching absorbs all latency.
No model at all — pure rule-based template completion.
optionExplanations: 70B 单次解码就可能超预算，堆算力也难在 100–150ms 内稳定完成。
对；100–150ms 的推理窗口把 inline 逼到 1–7B，再靠投机解码/KV cache 挤进预算。
缓存省的是重复 prefill，救不了大模型每 token 的解码延迟，越大越难达标。
纯规则补全覆盖不了真实代码的多样性，质量撑不起产品。
optionExplanations_en: A 70B's single decode can blow the budget; even with compute it's hard to finish reliably in 100–150ms.
Correct — the 100–150ms inference window forces inline to 1–7B, squeezed into budget by speculative decoding/KV cache.
Caching saves repeated prefill but can't fix a big model's per-token decode latency; bigger is harder to hit.
Pure rules can't cover real code's diversity; quality can't carry the product.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把最小的模型直接跑在用户机器上，彻底消除网络往返延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: On-device runs the smallest model directly on the user's machine, eliminating network round-trip latency.

tradeoff: 小模型（能进 100–150ms 但能力弱）vs 大模型（更准但超预算）

scenario: 推理只剩 100–150ms，要用哪些手段把模型塞进这个窗口。
scenario_en: Only 100–150ms remain for inference; which techniques fit the model into that window.
q: 为把 inline 推理压进延迟预算，可以用哪些手段？(多选)
q_en: Which techniques help fit inline inference into the latency budget? (multiple)
why: 小模型(1–7B)、speculative decoding、KV cache 复用 prefill、谨慎批处理都能压延迟；把 context 从 4K 加到 32K 只会抬高 prefill 成本，方向相反。
why_en: Small models, speculative decoding, KV caching for shared prefill, and careful batching all cut latency, while enlarging the context window only raises prefill and latency.
options: 用小模型(1–7B) + speculative decoding 加速解码
KV cache 管理，避免每次键入都重算 prefill
谨慎的请求批处理，避免排队推过延迟阈值
把 context window 从 4K 加到 32K，喂更多上下文
options_en: Use a small model (1–7B) plus speculative decoding to speed decode.
KV cache management to avoid recomputing prefill on every keystroke.
Careful request batching to avoid queuing past the latency threshold.
Grow the context window from 4K to 32K to feed more context.
optionExplanations: 对；小模型 + 投机解码直接缩短解码时间，是压进 100–150ms 的主力。
对；键入频繁、前缀高度重叠，KV cache 免重算 prefill 能省大量时间。
对；批处理要谨慎，攒太久反而排队超时，谨慎批处理是平衡吞吐与尾延迟。
错；上下文从 4K 涨到 32K 会让 prefill 成本暴涨、延迟飙升，与压预算背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a small model plus speculative decoding directly shortens decode, the main lever to fit 100–150ms.
Correct — with frequent keystrokes and highly overlapping prefixes, KV caching avoids recomputing prefill and saves a lot.
Correct — batching must be careful; over-collecting causes queuing timeouts, so careful batching balances throughput and tail latency.
Wrong — growing context 4K→32K explodes prefill cost and latency, opposite to fitting the budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 小草稿模型猜多 token、大模型一次前向验证，降低解码延迟且不掉质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Speculative decoding has a small draft model propose tokens the large model verifies in one pass, cutting decode latency with no quality loss.

scenario: 面试里主动提隐私：用户源码是敏感 IP，不能泄露给他人或未经同意拿去训练。
scenario_en: You raise privacy unprompted: user source is sensitive IP that must not leak to others or train models without consent.
q: 在代码补全系统里，隐私应被当作什么来对待？
q_en: How should privacy be treated in a code-completion system?
why: 隐私是「部署门槛(deployment gate)」而非可选功能：用户代码是敏感 IP，泄露或未授权训练会直接让企业拒绝采用。必须先满足隐私模式（telemetry-on/off、air-gapped）才谈得上落地，而不是事后加的加分项。
why_en: Privacy is a deployment gate, not a feature — leaking code or training on it without consent makes enterprises refuse adoption, so it must be satisfied before deployment.
options: 一个可选的加分功能，等产品先上线站稳脚跟之后再慢慢补上就行
一个部署门槛：不满足隐私模式，企业根本不会采用
只需要在训练阶段考虑数据来源，推理阶段传代码片段不用操心
纯粹是合规团队和法务的事，跟系统架构设计完全无关
options_en: An optional bonus feature you can bolt on later, once the product has launched and found its footing.
A deployment gate: without privacy modes, enterprises simply won't adopt.
Only a training-time data-sourcing concern; sending code snippets at inference needs no worry.
Purely a matter for the compliance and legal team, completely unrelated to system architecture.
optionExplanations: 当加分项事后补会直接卡住企业采用，隐私不满足就没有「以后」。
对；隐私是准入门槛，决定企业敢不敢用，必须前置进架构（部署模式）设计。
推理阶段照样在传输用户代码片段，隐私在推理侧同样是硬约束，不能只顾训练阶段。
隐私直接决定部署模式(云/本地/air-gapped)，深度影响架构，不只是合规法务的事。
optionExplanations_en: Treating it as a later bonus blocks enterprise adoption outright; without privacy there is no 'later.'
Correct — privacy is an admission gate deciding whether enterprises dare adopt, so it must be front-loaded into architecture (deployment modes).
Inference still transmits user code snippets, so privacy is a hard constraint on the inference side too, not just training.
Privacy dictates the deployment mode (cloud/on-prem/air-gapped), deeply shaping architecture, not just compliance and legal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 必须先满足才能落地的硬性前提，不满足就无法上线，而非可选功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deployment gate is a hard prerequisite that must be met to ship at all, not an optional feature.

scenario: 要为不同客户群设计三种隐私部署模式，从个人到强监管企业。
scenario_en: You must design three privacy deployment modes for customer tiers, from individuals to heavily regulated enterprises.
q: telemetry-on、telemetry-off、air-gapped 三种隐私模式各是什么？
q_en: What are the telemetry-on, telemetry-off, and air-gapped privacy modes?
why: 隐私强度递增：telemetry-on 发片段并可选保留（个人默认）；telemetry-off 只推理、不保留不训练（企业）；air-gapped 模型全本地、代码不出边界。
why_en: Telemetry-on sends snippets for inference and may retain them (default for individuals); telemetry-off does inference only with no retention/training; air-gapped keeps the model on-prem so code never leaves.
tradeoff: 隐私强度递增：telemetry-on < telemetry-off < air-gapped（越私越难改进模型/越贵）
options: 三者其实完全一样，只是产品市场部门为了卖不同价位而取了不同的名字
on 可选保留；off 只推理不保留；air-gapped 全本地
on 是最私密的模式、air-gapped 反而最开放，隐私强度逐级递减
三者其实都要把用户代码上传去训练模型，区别只在服务器部署的地理区域
options_en: The three are actually identical, just given different names by marketing to sell different price tiers.
On may retain; off is inference-only with no retention; air-gapped runs fully on-prem.
On is the most private mode and air-gapped is actually the most open — privacy decreases step by step.
All three actually upload user code to train the model and differ only in which geographic region the servers sit in.
optionExplanations: 三者在是否发送、是否保留、是否出边界上层层不同，绝非只是换个名字卖不同价位。
对；从可选保留到只推理再到全本地，隐私强度递增，正好覆盖个人到强监管客户。
隐私强度反了：on 最开放、air-gapped 最私，不是逐级递减。
off 和 air-gapped 明确不训练，air-gapped 连代码都不出边界，谈不上都上传训练。
optionExplanations_en: The three differ layer by layer on sending, retention, and leaving the boundary — not just renamed price tiers.
Correct — from optional retention to inference-only to fully on-prem, privacy increases, covering individuals to regulated customers.
Privacy direction reversed: on is most open, air-gapped most private — not a decreasing ladder.
Off and air-gapped explicitly don't train, and air-gapped keeps code inside the boundary, so 'all upload for training' is false.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只用代码片段做推理，不保留、不用于训练；企业常见要求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Telemetry-off uses snippets for inference only, with no retention or training — a common enterprise requirement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型完全部署在本地或客户云内，代码不离开客户安全边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Air-gapped deployment runs the model entirely on-prem or in the customer's cloud so code never leaves their boundary.

scenario: 客户是金融或国防这类强监管行业，明确要求源代码绝不能离开自己的边界。
scenario_en: The customer is a heavily regulated industry (finance/defense) that requires source code never leave its boundary.
q: 「代码绝不能出边界」的强监管客户该用哪种部署模式？
q_en: Which deployment mode fits a regulated customer whose code must never leave the boundary?
why: 硬约束是「代码零外传」：只有 air-gapped 把模型和推理整套放进客户边界内。telemetry-off 不保留，但片段仍要发到外部推理，跨了边界。
why_en: Air-gapped: the whole model runs on-prem or in the customer's cloud so inference happens inside the boundary and no code leaves, unlike telemetry-off which still sends snippets out.
whenOtherWins: 如果客户只要求「不被保留/不拿去训练」但可接受把片段发到外部做推理，telemetry-off 就够，air-gapped 的自建部署成本没必要。
options: telemetry-on，反正可以关掉保留
telemetry-off，只推理不保留就满足要求
air-gapped，模型全在客户边界内，代码零外传
多租户共享云，靠加密传输保证安全
options_en: Telemetry-on, since retention can be turned off anyway.
Telemetry-off, since inference-only with no retention meets it.
Air-gapped, with the whole model inside the customer's boundary and zero code egress.
Multi-tenant shared cloud, secured by encrypted transport.
optionExplanations: telemetry-on 仍会外发片段甚至保留，最不满足强监管的零外传要求。
只挡住了「保留」这一层，出站这一层没挡住；若客户只怕留痕它就够用。
对；推理跑在客户机房或私有云里，审计时能直接证明没有出站流量。
多租户共享云代码仍离开客户边界，加密传输也改变不了「出了边界」这一事实。
optionExplanations_en: Telemetry-on still egresses snippets and may retain them — the worst fit for a zero-egress regulated requirement.
It blocks retention but not egress; if the customer only fears traces being kept, it suffices.
Correct — inference runs inside the customer datacenter, so an audit can show zero outbound traffic.
Multi-tenant cloud still moves code outside the boundary; encryption doesn't change that it left.

termDefinitions.meaning: 如金融、国防，有严格数据不出境/不出边界的合规要求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regulated industry (e.g. finance, defense) has strict compliance that data must not leave its boundary.

tradeoff: air-gapped（零外传但客户自建、模型更新慢）vs telemetry-off（免运维但片段仍出站）

scenario: 企业客户因为「代码片段被保留、可能用于训练」而集体拒绝采用你的补全产品。
scenario_en: Enterprise customers collectively refuse to adopt your completion product because snippets are retained and may be used for training.
q: 企业因数据保留担忧拒绝采用，最直接的产品化解法是什么？
q_en: Enterprises refuse over retention concerns — what's the most direct product fix?
why: 企业的顾虑是「保留 + 训练」而不是「出站」；telemetry-off 从架构上砍掉这两件事，正是 Copilot for Business 的做法。
why_en: Offer a telemetry-off mode — inference only, no retention or training — which is exactly why GitHub added Copilot for Business, since enterprises refused otherwise.
whenOtherWins: 如果客户连「把片段发到外部推理」都不接受（强监管），telemetry-off 不够，得上 air-gapped 全本地部署。
options: telemetry-off：只推理、不保留、不训练
承诺给企业做口头保证说不会看他们的代码，但底层架构完全不变
把数据保留期从 90 天缩短到 30 天，保留机制本身照样存在
给企业客户打折，用更低的价格换取他们接受数据被保留
options_en: Telemetry-off: inference only, no retention, no training.
Give enterprises a verbal promise not to look at their code, while the underlying architecture stays exactly the same.
Shorten retention from 90 days to 30 days, while the retention mechanism itself still exists.
Give enterprise customers a discount, trading a lower price for accepting that data is retained.
optionExplanations: 对；它是合同和架构都能落地的最小改动，不必像 air-gapped 那样让客户自建集群。
口头保证没有架构约束背书，企业合规不会认，担忧依旧。
缩短保留期仍是「保留」，没消除「不希望被保留/训练」的根本顾虑。
打折不改变数据处理方式，企业要的是隐私保证不是折扣。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it is the smallest change that both contracts and architecture can honor, without making the customer run their own cluster.
A verbal promise has no architectural backing; enterprise compliance won't accept it and the concern remains.
Shortening retention is still retention, not removing the core 'don't retain/train' concern.
A discount doesn't change data handling; enterprises want a privacy guarantee, not a price cut.

termDefinitions.meaning: GitHub 面向企业的版本，加入 telemetry-off 以满足不保留/不训练要求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Copilot for Business is GitHub's enterprise tier that added telemetry-off to meet no-retention/no-training needs.

tradeoff: telemetry-off（改动小、仍走外部推理）vs air-gapped（零外传但客户要自建部署）

scenario: 你的模型用公共 GitHub 仓库训练，其中混有 GPL/AGPL 等 copyleft 许可证的代码。
scenario_en: Your model trains on public GitHub repos, some under GPL/AGPL copyleft licenses.
q: 用公共仓库训练带来的法律风险是什么，怎么缓解？
q_en: What legal risk comes from training on public repos, and how do you mitigate it?
why: copyleft（GPL/AGPL）有传染性衍生条款：输出与受限代码雷同时，可能给用户的专有代码套上许可义务。缓解是引用追踪，接受前先审。
why_en: Copyleft (GPL/AGPL) has viral derivative-work terms that can impose license obligations if output matches restricted training code, mitigated by reference tracking that flags suggestions resembling known licensed code.
tradeoff: 用全部公共代码（数据多但 copyleft 法律风险）vs 过滤+引用追踪（合规但语料缩水）
options: 风险是模型体积太大，缓解靠 int8 量化压缩
copyleft 传染专有代码；靠引用追踪标记雷同
风险是训练太慢，缓解靠多卡 data parallel
公共仓库没有任何法律风险，可随意用于训练
options_en: The risk is the model being too big, mitigated by int8 quantization.
Copyleft can infect proprietary code; reference tracking flags look-alike suggestions.
The risk is slow training, mitigated by multi-GPU data parallelism.
Public repos carry no legal risk and can be used freely for training.
optionExplanations: 模型大小是工程问题，跟许可证传染的法律风险无关。
对；风险在「输出雷同」那一刻发生，所以缓解要卡在接受前的提示，而不是训练后补救。
训练速度与许可证风险无关，答非所问。
公共≠无版权，很多公共仓库带 copyleft 许可，直接用有真实法律风险。
optionExplanations_en: Model size is an engineering issue, unrelated to license-contamination legal risk.
Correct — the risk materializes the moment output resembles restricted code, so the mitigation must sit before acceptance, not after training.
Training speed is unrelated to license risk — off point.
Public isn't copyright-free; many public repos carry copyleft, so using them directly has real legal risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 如 GPL/AGPL 的许可证，要求衍生作品沿用同样开放条款，具传染性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Copyleft (e.g. GPL/AGPL) requires derivative works to keep the same open terms — a viral obligation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当模型建议与已知受限代码高度相似时标记出来，供开发者审查许可义务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reference tracking flags when a suggestion closely matches known licensed code so developers review license obligations.

scenario: 同一道 Copilot 系统设计题，L4、L5、Staff+ 的作答范围与深度不同。
scenario_en: For the same Copilot design prompt, L4, L5, and Staff+ differ in scope and depth.
q: 从 L4 到 Staff+，作答这道题的关键升级是什么？
q_en: From L4 to Staff+, what's the key escalation in answering this prompt?
why: L4 定一个入口 + 基础架构；L5 列全四入口、讲取舍、主动提隐私；Staff+ 当平台做：指标绑收入、三种隐私架构、接受→改进反馈环。
why_en: L4 scopes inline with acceptance rate; L5 enumerates all surfaces with trade-offs, full metric hierarchy, latency breakdown, and unprompted privacy; Staff+ frames it as a platform tying every decision to business outcomes.
tradeoff: L4（单入口+基础）vs L5（全入口+取舍+隐私）vs Staff+（平台化+指标绑收入+反馈环）
options: L4 用更大模型、Staff+ 反而用更小模型省钱，唯一差别就是模型规模大小
L4 单入口+基础架构；L5 全入口+取舍+隐私；Staff+ 平台化
L4 只谈业务价值、Staff+ 只谈技术细节，两者完全不重叠、互不搭边
级别越高答得越笼统抽象，Staff+ 只讲宏大愿景，从不落地到具体细节
options_en: L4 uses bigger models and Staff+ smaller ones to save cost; model size is the only difference.
L4: one surface + basics; L5: all surfaces + trade-offs + privacy; Staff+: platform.
L4 talks only business value and Staff+ only technical detail, with zero overlap between the two.
Higher levels answer ever more vaguely; Staff+ only pitches a grand vision and never gets to concrete detail.
optionExplanations: 级别差别不在模型大小，而在 scoping 广度、取舍深度和业务联系。
对；从单入口基础，到全入口+隐私+取舍，再到平台化+收入+反馈环，是逐级加宽加深。
Staff+ 恰恰把技术决策全接到业务结果上，不是只谈技术、跟业务不搭边，二分错误。
级别越高越具体、越把决策落到业务，不是越笼统抽象。
optionExplanations_en: The level gap isn't model size but scoping breadth, trade-off depth, and business linkage.
Correct — from one surface + basics, to all surfaces + privacy + trade-offs, to platform + revenue + feedback loops, progressively broader and deeper.
Staff+ specifically connects every technical decision to business outcomes, not tech-only with zero business overlap — the dichotomy is wrong.
Higher levels get more concrete and business-grounded, not vaguer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试里主动划定要设计什么、深挖哪块、为什么，体现级别的关键动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scoping is proactively bounding what to design and what to deep-dive and why — a key level-signaling move in interviews.

scenario: 要给这道题一个 Staff+ 的框法，而不是只答某一个入口。
scenario_en: You want a Staff+ framing for this prompt rather than answering just one surface.
q: Staff+ 会怎么框这道代码补全题？
q_en: How would a Staff+ candidate frame this code-completion problem?
why: 把它当共享基础设施上服务多入口的平台：指标绑到订阅收入，三种隐私模式各有架构，再建「接受信号→模型改进」的反馈环。
why_en: As a platform serving multiple surfaces on shared infrastructure, with metrics tied to revenue (retention→subscription), privacy architecture for all three modes, and an acceptance→model-improvement feedback loop.
options: 只把 inline 做到极致，其余入口不提
当作服务多入口的平台：指标绑收入、建反馈环
只讨论选哪个开源模型，其余交给别人
只给出一张架构图，不谈指标和业务
options_en: Perfect inline only and never mention other surfaces.
Treat it as a platform serving several surfaces: metrics tied to revenue, plus a feedback loop.
Only debate which open-source model to pick, leaving the rest to others.
Only draw one architecture diagram, no metrics or business.
optionExplanations: 只做 inline 是 L4/L5 的 scoping，不是把多入口统一到平台的 Staff+ 视角。
对；平台化 + 指标绑收入 + 隐私架构 + 反馈环，把技术全接到业务结果，是 Staff+ 的标志。
选模型只是一个子决策，撑不起平台级框法。
只给架构图不谈指标业务，恰恰缺了 Staff+ 最看重的业务联系。
optionExplanations_en: Inline only is L4/L5 scoping, not the Staff+ view unifying surfaces into a platform.
Correct — platform-izing plus revenue-tied metrics plus privacy architecture plus a feedback loop connects tech to business, the Staff+ hallmark.
Picking a model is one sub-decision and can't carry a platform-level framing.
A diagram with no metrics or business misses exactly the business linkage Staff+ values most.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个入口视为共享基础设施上的统一平台来设计，而非孤立功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platform framing designs multiple surfaces as one unified platform on shared infrastructure, not isolated features.

q: 把一次 inline 请求在 200ms 预算内的时间开销按发生顺序排好：
q_en: Order the time costs of one inline request within the 200ms budget:
steps: IDE 插件收集前缀/后缀/开着的标签页(约 10–30ms)
序列化请求经网络送到推理服务器(约 20–50ms 往返)
模型 prefill + 自回归解码(约 100–150ms)
建议以 ghost text 返回 IDE，等待用户 Tab 接受
why: 顺序：IDE 收上下文(10–30ms) → 网络往返(20–50ms) → prefill+解码(100–150ms) → 返回 ghost text。前两步吃掉 30–80ms，推理只剩 100–150ms。
why_en: Collect context in the IDE (10–30ms), send over the network (20–50ms round-trip), run prefill + decode (100–150ms), then return the ghost text — the first ~30–80ms is gone before compute.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["收集上下文
10-30ms"] --> N["网络往返
20-50ms"] N --> M["prefill+解码
100-150ms"] M --> R["ghost text 返回"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 以灰色预览显示的 inline 建议，用户按 Tab 才落地为真实代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ghost text is the grey inline suggestion preview that becomes real code only when the user presses Tab.
